capabilities.description: Administrator-only delivery of Silo notifications, playback events, watchdog and failure alerts.
Administrator-only Gotify connection and alert settings.

Checks Silo's stream nodes, restart state, database and Redis, and the server's disk and memory, and sends a Gotify alert (and a recovery alert) to admins who turned it on. Needs the Silo administrator API key. Suggested schedule: every 5 minutes.

Sends admins who turned it on a Gotify summary of the last 7 days: plays, time watched, top viewers and top titles. Each admin picks their own day and hour (default Sunday 18:00, in their time zone) and a run sends it in that hour or in any later run within 6 hours after (so a week isn't lost if Silo was down), at most once a week, so schedule it to run every hour. Needs the Silo administrator API key. Suggested schedule: every 1 hour.

Checks newly added movies and episodes with a resumable catalog cursor. Suggested schedule: every 2 minutes. No initial library flood. Requires the Silo administrator API key. Posters/overview depend on host availability.

presentation.summary: Administrator-only Silo notifications through Gotify: playback, watchdogs, failures and server health.
presentation.description_markdown:
![Surify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deejayexe/silo-plugin-suricata/main/plugins/surify/web/surify-logo.webp)

Send Silo notifications to a self-hosted Gotify server. Administrator notifications, episode grouping, quiet hours, custom templates, playback and failure alerts, stream watchdogs, server health and recovery checks, weekly digests and links to Silo’s native activity page. Uses Silo events and one administrator API key for Silo queries and stream-control actions. Adapted from the MIT-licensed plugin by Josh Black. Gotify uses application tokens, Markdown links and priorities 0, 2, 5, 8 and 10. Sounds and device selection are managed in the Gotify client. New library content can include a Markdown poster and Android big image when Silo exposes a usable image URL. Repeating alerts and binary poster uploads are not supported. Access is restricted to administrators on their primary profile. Other users cannot see the navigation entry or access the pages/API. Before background delivery, Silo must confirm the recipient is still an enabled administrator. Connections from older builds remain inactive until saved by the administrator after upgrading.
presentation.setup_markdown:
1. Sign in to Silo as an administrator on your primary profile. Open Surify from the administrator navigation.
2. Create a Gotify application and copy its private application token (legacy or gtfya.…). Save the server URL and token on the Connection tab. After upgrading from an earlier build, save the existing connection once to activate administrator-only delivery.
3. Check the server and send a test notification.
4. Save one unrestricted Silo administrator API key. The same key handles monitoring, recipient checks and stream-control actions. It stays hidden, and Surify does not create or revoke keys. Live sessions are available in Silo’s native Admin > Activity page.
5. Configure server alerts. Bind health_check to every 5 minutes and weekly_digest to every hour, then restart Silo after changing task bindings. Ordinary users and secondary profiles cannot access this plugin.
6. For the new library content alert, enable New library content in Server alerts, bind recently_added to an interval of 2 minutes, and restart Silo after changing the binding. Existing library items are not announced. Artwork uses public/resolved Silo URLs when available.
